subject: Food Science
title: Natural vs. Artificial
description: A short lesson to help you apply Natural vs. Artificial.

hook.text: Vanilla extract from orchids and vanillin from wood pulp taste identical. One costs 20 times more.

buildup.text: 'Natural' and 'artificial' labels imply safety differences. Chemically, the molecules are often the same.

discovery.text: Natural flavors can require 50+ chemical solvents to extract. The process isn't always simpler or safer.

twist.text: Cyanide is natural. Arsenic is natural. 'Natural' doesn't equal safe—and 'artificial' doesn't equal dangerous.

climax.text: Consumer demand for 'natural' labels costs the industry $40 billion annually—often for identical chemistry.

punchline.text: Same molecule, different story. Nature is a brand, not a safety standard.

quiz.question: How do natural vanilla extract and artificial vanillin compare chemically?
options: Identical molecules—one just costs 20 times more
